earlier_scan.source_named: Avram, Andrei A. 2010. An outline of Romanian Pidgin Arabic. Journal of Language Contact 3(1): 20-38 (grammar sketch; paywalled at Brill).

sources.citation: Avram, Andrei A. 2010. An outline of Romanian Pidgin Arabic. Journal of Language Contact 3(2) [VARIA 3]: 20-38. DOI 10.1163/19552629-90000018 (also 10.1163/000000010792317884). Brill, free access.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 2 'Phonology' (pp. 21-22) treats only inter-speaker variation, loss of vowel length, and consonant substitutions (pharyngeals, emphatics, velar fricatives, /q/, degemination, /p v/ > /b/); it says nothing about stress. The only mention is in section 4 'The lexicon', p. 32, on lexical hybrids: 'problem [proˈblem].. cf. E. problem and Rom. problemă [proˈbleməә]' and 'The form in (45d), while very similar to English, has the stress pattern of its Romanian counterpart'; (45e) duktur [duk'tur]. No rule for where word stress falls.

sources.note: Earlier, shorter version of the same description (fieldwork 1984-85). Section 2 'Phonology' pp. 13-15 is segmental only. p. 23 (lexicon): 'The form in (45d) ends in [m], as in English, but has the stress pattern of its Romanian counterpart' (problem [pro'blem]). No general stress statement.
